scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Siguiriyas dates back to the late 18th century as part of the cante jondo tradition in Andalusia, with origins firmly rooted in Romani (Calé) culture.
Early forms were performed a cappella like tonás, later developing guitar accompaniment.

Key historical figures like the 19th-century cantaor El Planeta and his disciple El Fillo shaped its early classics, while the 1922 Concurso de Cante Jondo in Granada helped preserve its archaic forms through performers like El Tenazas and Manolo Caracol.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Embodying the quintessence of jondura and cante puro, siguiriyas addresses profound human suffering, tragic love, imprisonment, and death.
Historically linked to wake settings and serious artistic presentations.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Introduced by Vicente Escudero in 1940, the dance is solemn, ceremonious, and pausado, lacking external ornamentation.
The formal progression moves from a guitar and singer introduction to an entrada, initial letra, escobilla, second letra, danced falseta, and a final escobilla.
Footwork and counter-rhythms interlock with the compás.
Watch for Escobilla.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Played in A Phrygian with a 12-count compás featuring accents on beats 1, 3, 5, 8, and 11.
It utilizes guitar, palmas, and dancer footwork.

scenes.title: The people
narration: El Planeta (credited with the oldest style), El Fillo, Frasco el Colorao, La Niña de los Peines, Vicente Escudero (who introduced the dance in 1940), Paco La Luz, Silverio Franconetti, Diego Bermúdez Cala ('El Tenazas'), and Manolo Caracol.
Variants differ across Andalusian regions: Cádiz features simple, unornamented styles (El Planeta), while Triana offers highly ornate interpretations (Frasco el Colorao, La Niña de los Peines).
Derived from primitive tonás.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: siguiriyas is sibling of soleares: Shares a 12-beat framework with an inverted accent structure.
siguiriyas is parent of tonás: Oldest forms of siguiriyas derive directly from primitive tonás.
siguiriyas is variant of serranas: Rigorously governed by the compás propio de la seguiriya.
siguiriyas is variant of livianas: Operates under the same seguiriya compás style.
